topics.label: Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, audience background, and core learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Differentiation and Tissue Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes cause cells to fail their normal developmental programs and disrupt structured tissue architecture.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the histological and biological differences between benign and malignant tumors through the mechanisms of local invasion and distant metastasis.

topics.label: Neoplasm Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard naming rules, tissue suffixes, and exceptions used to classify benign and malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Pathophysiology and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physical and systemic mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause morbidity and patient death.

topics.label: Cancer Incidence and Comparative Oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the distribution of tumor types across human tissues and illustrate cancer occurrence across diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Clinical Presentation and Cancer Screening Modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, histological detection methods, and relative effectiveness of population screening for various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation by reviewing the learning outcomes and giving practical reminders.
